item.title: Speakers
item.description:
Keynote speakers

We are delighted to announce the following speakers for scverse conference 2026, with more to be confirmed.

Phil Ewels

Seqera

Product Manager for Open Source at Seqera, with a PhD in Molecular Biology from the University of Cambridge. He previously worked at the National Genomics Infrastructure (SciLifeLab, Stockholm) and the Babraham Institute in Cambridge. Phil co-founded the nf-core community and authored MultiQC, RustQC, and SRA-Explorer, and is a passionate advocate for user-friendly open-source software.

item.title: Registration
item.description:
Registration is now open — sign up here.

Registration

Registration for scverse conference 2026 is now open. Register here. Capacity is limited, so we recommend registering early.

Sign up for announcements via Zulip or follow us on social media for the latest updates.

Travel grants

We are committed to making the conference accessible to as many people as possible. As in previous years, we plan to offer travel grants to help cover registration, accommodation, and travel.

item.title: Call for proposals
item.description:
Abstract submission is open until September 7, 2026 — submit here.

Share your work

The scverse conference program is built with the community. We welcome submissions from researchers, developers, and users across the single-cell and spatial omics ecosystem. Submission types include:

Talks

Present your research, tool, or method as a contributed talk. Selected abstracts are scheduled across the main program.

Posters

Share work in progress and connect with the community during dedicated poster sessions.

item.title: Sponsors
item.description:
Partner with scverse

scverse® builds the foundational, interoperable open-source tools for single-cell and spatial omics — including Scanpy, AnnData, squidpy, and scvi-tools — used by labs worldwide and described in journals such as Nature Biotechnology. scverse is a non-profit, fiscally sponsored project of NumFOCUS.

The annual scverse conference sits at the intersection of academia and industry, bringing together developers, academic labs, and researchers at every career stage. Your sponsorship funds the community directly — travel grants, fee waivers, and free tools, not shareholders.

item.title: Venue & travel
item.description:
Venue

The conference is hosted at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), just north of Copenhagen. The exact buildings and rooms will be confirmed closer to the event.

Detailed venue, room, and map information to be announced.

Getting to Copenhagen

By air

Copenhagen Airport (CPH) is the main international gateway, well connected across Europe and beyond, with a direct metro and train link to the city centre.

By train

Copenhagen is connected by rail to the rest of Denmark, Sweden (via the Øresund Bridge), and continental Europe.

item.title: Code of Conduct
item.description:
This code of conduct was developed for the scverse conferences. For more details, see the full scverse Code of Conduct.

Our pledge

We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

item.title: Organizers
item.description:
Organizing committee

The scverse conference 2026 is organised by members of the scverse community together with our local hosts at DTU, Copenhagen. The full committee will be listed here soon.

Organizing committee to be announced.

Get involved

The conference is a community effort. If you would like to help organise, volunteer during the event, or host a satellite session, reach out to us at conference2026@scverse.org.

You can also learn more about the people behind scverse on the People page and about the project on our About page.
